A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture and higher-dimensional Gaussian sampling simulations, including bias and mixing-speed results in Section 4 and Figures 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original sampling simulations and their reported outcomes in Section 4 and Figures 1–5.

M1.justification: The noise-corrected Langevin updates and step-size constraint in Eqs. (6)–(8) are unchanged. Half-denoising retains the same procedure; its equations move from (10)–(11) to (15)–(16).

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate two-dimensional Gaussian mixtures with 1–4 components and white Gaussian distributions in 5, 10, and 100 dimensions, with the same noise conditions. Appendix E adds mathematical analysis of the existing Gaussian setting.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain Basic Langevin, Oracle Langevin, their quarter-step-size variants, and exact-sampling ground truth. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain one million sampling steps, analysis of the final 30%, the same density-estimation bandwidth and grid spacing, and the same distance metrics. The mixing study still uses 10,000 trials of 100 steps with the same initialization.

E4.justification: The experimental step-size sensitivity comparisons and mixing-speed analysis remain unchanged in Section 4 and Figures 3–5. The added Gaussian appendix develops theoretical bias and convergence results without adding an empirical ablation or robustness study.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains standard-error bars, and Figure 5 retains averaging over 10,000 runs. Neither version provides additional seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 1–5 retain identical plot content and simulation outcomes. The findings remain that half-denoising approaches Oracle Langevin at matched step sizes, improves upon Basic Langevin, and preserves mixing speed.

T1.justification: v1's Theorem 2 establishes approximate stationarity with O(µ²) residuals while leaving regularity conditions unspecified. v2 replaces this with an explicitly conditioned, higher-order comparison to Oracle Langevin and substantially rewrites the proof. It adds a Langevin/deconvolution derivation, a proof of Corollary 1, supporting lemmas, and Gaussian stationary-covariance and convergence analyses in Appendices B–E.

C1.justification: The single-noise-level sampling and half-denoising contributions remain unchanged. The conclusion qualifies v1's claim to prove convergence by instead describing convergence analysis through equivalence to Oracle Langevin.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds a mechanism explanation through ordinary Langevin dynamics for noisy iterates and substantially develops applicability qualifications: bounded scores, smoothness, comparison at the target distribution, and conjectural third-order accuracy. Appendix E adds interpretations separating noisy-score bias from finite-step bias and states the Gaussian initialization and step-size conditions for covariance convergence.

D1.justification: The documented sampling, initialization, and density-estimation details are retained. v2 adds no implementation, hardware, training-time, or code/data-access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hurault et al. (2025), Ma et al. (2015), Zhang et al. (2022), and Deasy et al. (2021). These additions distinguish noisy score estimates from scores of noisy data and identify Gaussian error analysis and non-Gaussian DSM as related directions.

P1.justification: Terminology changes from 'noisy score' to 'noisy-data score,' with localized wording and explanatory edits. Section 3 separates the algorithm, theoretical analysis, and half-denoising, and the appendices are reorganized. Most existing narrative and experimental exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: All five figures retain their graphical content. Figures 1 and 2 move from a shared page to separate pages, and surrounding text, captions, equations, and references reflow. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Explicit assumptions, more qualified convergence wording, and Appendix E's Gaussian covariance and convergence analysis improve upon v1's approximate-stationarity treatment. However, the expanded proofs contain algebraic inconsistencies: Eq. (33) has an incorrect score-difference expansion, and Eq. (45) has the opposite sign from the retained Tweedie formula. The clearer scope and independent Gaussian analysis provide a limited net improvement, while these errors limit the gain in theoretical reliability.
